1	# Every duplicated or asserted fact carries a mechanical drift-guard to its canonical source
     2	
     3	**Status:** accepted (design ratified 2026-07-08; implemented by the spec and plan below; amended
     4	2026-08-02 — a file-disjoint guard/mirror split takes a `deps` edge, not shared-wave placement — and
     5	2026-08-19 — the touched-doc scope widening; corrected 2026-08-20 — the glossary term count is owned
     6	by the live subsection; see the amendments and the correction below)
     7	
     8	WAR is riddled with facts stated in one surface that live canonically in another and rot silently
     9	against ground truth because **nothing binds the copy to its source**. The failure is uniform: a green
    10	gate, a green audit, and a green `node --test` run all pass identically whether the two surfaces agree
    11	or have drifted, because every existing check is either *presence-only* ("this surface contains the
    12	anchor phrase") or *well-formedness-only* ("this JSON parses"). Drift stays invisible until a manual doc
    13	sweep re-diffs the referents by hand — the exact labor this repo keeps paying. Twelve recorded frictions
    14	are one class through twelve lenses: inlined constants the Workflow sandbox cannot `import` and that land
    15	without their guard (`HARD_ESCALATION_REASONS`, `KNOWN_LAND_DECISIONS`, and the `war-config.mjs` roster
    16	helpers mirrored into `workflow-template.js`); the two behavior surfaces per agent (standing `agents/*.md`
    17	vs the dispatched prompts string-built in `workflow-template.js`, with the gate-audit seats building
    18	prompts inline outside `auditPrompt()`); presence-not-identity doc contracts (the CLAUDE.md pointer line
    19	asserted merely *present* per surface, never *equal* across them); default-flip and preset doc rot; four
    20	version slots bumped by convention with no cross-slot check; and prose asserting code facts with no guard
    21	(ADR policy-table under-attribution, comments lagging a rewrite, a `held:*` classifier example
    22	contradicting its own routing predicate, a "shell out to X" idiom mislabeling an in-process export, a
    23	tour step freezing a false structural count). Full mechanics:
    24	[the design spec](../specs/2026-07-08-drift-guards-for-mirrored-and-asserted-facts-design.md) and
    25	[the plan](../plans/2026-07-08-drift-guards-for-mirrored-and-asserted-facts.md).
    26	
    27	## Decision
    28	
    29	**Every fact WAR duplicates across surfaces, or asserts in prose about a canonical code construct,
    30	carries a mechanical test that binds it to its canonical source — extraction + equality (`deepEqual` /
    31	byte-`===`), never presence.** A presence check (asserting an anchor phrase exists) or a well-formedness
    32	check (asserting JSON parses) is explicitly *not* a drift-guard and does not discharge the obligation.
    33	The guard reads the canonical source — a code export, a JSON field, a routing predicate — and the mirror
    34	site, and asserts they are equal; it anchors both targets by regex/name extraction, never line number
    35	(repo law — line numbers rot across the serial merge queue).
    36	
    37	Where a fact resists a cheap mechanical bind, there are exactly two ratified escapes, and prose-hope is
    38	not one of them:
    39	
    40	1. **Rewrite the fact so it cannot rot.** Narrative/tour prose asserts the *invariant* and names the
    41	   guard that holds it ("these arrays are kept identical by the mirror-registry drift-guard"), never the
    42	   snapshot count/divergence that rots ("differ by exactly one entry"). This extends the existing "cite
    43	   the section that DEFINES a mechanism" discipline to narrative prose.
    44	2. **Make the obligation an explicit, checkable auditor-lens duty.** Where grep structurally cannot see
    45	   the drift (ADR policy-table *under*-attribution; a comment lagging a rewrite), the check becomes a
    46	   standing duty on the auditor's cascading-impact lens, mirrored onto both its standing card and its
    47	   dispatched prompt — not a hope, and not a blocking script that would fire on every incidental rename.
    48	
    49	**The registries are the deliberate ceiling.** The set of guarded (canonical → mirror) pairs is an
    50	**explicit mirror registry**, and the set of correctness-critical both-surface directives is an
    51	**explicit both-surfaces directive registry** — each a listed set; adding a mirror or a directive means
    52	adding a row. This is the ratified alternative to a generic AST/import-graph scanner that would
    53	auto-discover every inline copy of every export: that scanner is a research project whose failure mode is
    54	a false sense of coverage (`// ponytail:` the registry as the ceiling; upgrade only on recurrence). The
    55	residual gap — a NEW mirror landing without a registry row — is closed by doctrine, not code: a
    56	`/war-strategy` plan-authoring rule (a mirror and its registry row land as one task) and a `/red-team`
    57	spine probe, exercised at every conversion and every red-team.
    58	
    59	This supersedes the byte-identity-by-convention posture of the pointer-line and version-slot conventions
    60	recorded in `CLAUDE.md` / `## Commands`: those conventions are now mechanically enforced (a cross-surface
    61	byte-identity test; a four-slot lock-step test), not honored by hand.
    62	
    63	## Relationship to prior ADRs
    64	
    65	- **Operates within [ADR 0017](0017-packaging-floor-docker-gate-ratified-backstops.md) — a drift-guard
    66	  is a *gate member*.** ADR 0017 requires every validation to live in the gate, a floor, or the ratified
    67	  backstops section, or the Lead escalates. A drift-guard is mechanical gate enforcement, which ADR 0017
    68	  prefers over prose; the residual per-change checks (default-flip OLD-absent, comment-lag) are declared
    69	  **backstops** with named runners (the `/war-strategy` rule, the red-team probe, the auditor lens),
    70	  never waived in prose.
    71	- **Leaves [ADR 0005](0005-dead-phase-halts-the-dag.md) untouched** — the mirror registry *reads*
    72	  `HARD_ESCALATION_REASONS` and `KNOWN_LAND_DECISIONS` as canonical; it adds **no** new status,
    73	  `HARD_ESCALATION_REASONS`, or `KNOWN_LAND_DECISIONS` member, so the hand-mirrored enum and its
    74	  discipline are byte-unchanged.
    75	- **Leaves [ADR 0006](0006-deterministic-test-floor.md) and
    76	  [ADR 0013](0013-commanders-intent-and-disposition-routing.md) untouched** — new drift-guards ride the
    77	  existing deterministic gate (0006); the auditor-lens duties route by the existing `disposition`
    78	  mechanism (0013), adding no new routing axis.
    79	- Historical ADRs are superseded, never edited.
    80	
    81	## Considered options
    82	
    83	- **One ADR versus twelve per-friction records (chosen: one).** The twelve recorded frictions are one
    84	  policy seen through twelve lenses; recording the discipline once — with the two-registry ceiling and
    85	  the two escape rules — keeps the "why extraction, why a registry, why prose is not enough" rationale in
    86	  one place.
    87	- **A generic AST / import-graph scanner (rejected — the registry is the ceiling).** Auto-discovering
    88	  every inline copy of every canonical export is a research project whose failure mode is a false sense
    89	  of coverage. Explicit registries plus a `/war-strategy` rule plus a red-team probe are the ratified
    90	  ceiling; the scanner is revisited only if unguarded-mirror recurrences continue after this lands.
    91	- **A blocking comment-lag script (rejected — advisory / auditor-lens).** "Old term" is per-change; a
    92	  blocking `.test.sh` would fire on every incidental rename (a poor gate citizen — the gate is
    93	  pass/fail). Comment-lag is a worker-prompt directive plus the auditor's cascading-impact lens, not a
    94	  script.
    95	
    96	## Consequences
    97	
    98	- A mirror and its registry row land as **one task** — an unguarded new mirror is a plan defect the
    99	  `/war-strategy` rule and the red-team spine probe reject.
   100	- The four release slots (`plugin.json#version`, `marketplace.json#metadata.version`,
   101	  `marketplace.json#plugins[0].version`, `README.md ## Status`) gain a fail-closed lock-step test; a
   102	  partial bump now turns the gate red instead of shipping a silently inconsistent release.
   103	- `CONTEXT.md` gains a `### Drift-guard discipline` subsection defining five terms — **Drift-guard**,
   104	  **Canonical source vs mirror site**, **Mirror registry**, **Both-surfaces directive registry**,
   105	  **Mechanism-style narrative**.
   106	- The doctrine ships to marketplace-pinned users via a version bump of the four release slots.
   107	- Named residual: mechanical detection of a *missing* registry row is out of scope (the rejected AST
   108	  scanner) — the doctrine's forcing functions are the plan-authoring rule and the red-team probe,
   109	  exercised from this plan onward.
   110	
   111	## Amendment (2026-08-02): a file-disjoint guard/mirror split resolves via a `deps` edge, not shared-wave placement
   112	
   113	The Decision above requires a mirror and its registry row to land as **one task**. When the guard
   114	file is already owned by a different task in the same phase — file-disjointness forbids the
   115	mirror-authoring task from touching it — the resolution is a **`deps` edge from the guard task onto
   116	the mirror-authoring task**, not "same phase, same wave, so they land together." Same phase and
   117	same wave are insufficient by themselves: every task worktree in a phase is cut from **one frozen
   118	phase base** at the Provision barrier, and waves order only *when* workers run, never *what base
   119	they see* (this repo's `CLAUDE.md`, "Execution architecture"). A guard task that merely shares a
   120	wave with — but carries no `deps` edge onto — the task authoring the fact it guards implements and
   121	is audited against a base that does not yet contain that fact: its own new guard row is red by
   122	construction, through no fault of the guard's diff.
   123	
   124	This is not a new escape hatch from the one-task rule: the guard task and the mirror-authoring task
   125	remain genuinely file-disjoint, so the `deps` edge encodes a **content** dependency the downstream
   126	task's worker discharges by rebasing onto the integration tip as its first act. It is explicitly
   127	*not* the forbidden "use `deps`/waves to dodge a same-file collision" this repo's decomposition
   128	rules warn against.
   129	
   130	Three forcing functions now carry the rule onto every plan-authoring path: (1) the `/red-team`
   131	universal spine probe `guard-split-deps-edge` (`skills/red-team/SKILL.md` and
   132	`references/lenses.md` §Drift-guard spine probes) flags an unedged split as a plan defect
   133	(`needsDecision`) at every conversion and every red-team; (2) the `/war-machine`
   134	**Guard-split deps-edge directive** (`skills/war-machine/SKILL.md`) makes the drafter add the edge
   135	before red-team ever sees the plan; (3) `/war-strategy` §3's Drift-guard coverage subsection
   136	carries the same rule as its authoring rule 7 (`skills/war-strategy/SKILL.md`), so a plan authored
   137	or converted outside `/war-machine` gets the same forcing function. See
   138	[[guard-task-split-from-mirror-task-needs-deps-edge-same-wave-insufficient]] for the full
   139	recurrence record this amendment closes.
   140	
   141	## Amendment (2026-08-19): the touched-doc scope widening — every touched-doc fact takes guard, de-mirror, or an explicit defer
   142	
   143	The Decision above binds facts WAR *duplicates across surfaces* or *asserts in prose about a canonical

38-- **Scope-lock preamble** — the scaffold prepends a hard preamble to **every** probe (spine *and* bespoke) and confirm: ignore the session cwd, the only subject is the fingerprinted plan + `repo`, executed probes work in a throwaway *copy* of `repo`, analyzed probes restrict reads to `repo`, and STOP if the opened plan's title differs. **Bespoke probe authors:** you get this for free, but still write your gist to name the absolute `repo`/`planFile`.
39-- **Provision step (executed probes)** — when the Lead passes a `provision` list (the pinned, repo-derived setup commands — see Part B's `provision.mjs` / setup-scout), the scope-lock additionally directs every **executed** probe to run those commands **in the sandbox copy, before the baseline**, bringing the tree to a gate-ready state (submodules, dependency install, …). Provisioning is environment setup, not the artifact under test: a **failing** provision step is an env-gap → `status:"warn"` + a note, and is **never** a red/fail verdict (a broken environment must not be mis-scored as a broken plan).
